name: Aged Shou Mei
categoryNote: White tea is withered and dried. Withering is the process — there is no kill-green. Ageing is time on that withered leaf, not a pile.

harvest.window: originally late spring or autumn leaf, then years

pluckStandard: later leaf, usually pressed, then stored dry for years

transformation.note: Slow change in a dry cake. Not 渥堆. The darker cup is time on a white tea, which is why this bar is taller than young Shou Mei and not hatched as microbial.

processing.description: Later leaf, long wither, dry. The extra process is storage.
White-tea path; often pressed so the cake can be kept as a project.
Years in a dry cabinet. Damp cupboards are mould. The storage guide’s line applies: most teas are food; this one is a project.

profile.mouthfeel: thicker, red-amber, low bitterness if stored dry

rinses.notes: optional rinse on a pressed cake; the drinking curve starts after

decoction.when: after the session, or as a separate pot of the last leaves
decoction.notes: 煮茶 — aged white will take a simmer. Young Yin Zhen will not thank you for this.

water.note: Boiling, with some mineral. The cake has already done the delicate years.

storage: Keep dry. This is already the project; wet-stored sourness is not “aged character”.

shelfLife.window: continues to change if actually dry
shelfLife.note: Most teas are food. A few teas are projects.

qualityMarkers.claim: harvest year and storage story that match

commonFaults.name: young Shou Mei at aged prices

compare.differentiator: Same wither-only make. Age is the second process. Young Shou Mei is herb-hay; this is date and amber.

summary: Shou Mei after the years: a dry-stored white cake that drinks as dates and amber, still not a pile-fermented dark tea.
